summary.short: Amends the definitions in KRS 154.20-220 for a Kentucky economic-development incentive for qualified data center projects, covering eligible companies, data center equipment, minimum capital investment, and memorandum-of-agreement terms of up to 50 years. Sections 19-24, 26, 35-37 take effect 1 July 2025.
summary.long: Partial text: Section 34 (definitions in KRS 154.20-220 to 154.20-229) and the Section 40 effective-date clause; Sections 1-33 and 35-39 are omitted. The Kentucky Economic Development Finance Authority enters memoranda of agreement with eligible companies (preliminary approval) and verifies that the minimum capital investment is made by the fifth anniversary (final approval). Eligible companies include owners, operators, colocation tenants and project organizers. Eligible costs cover purchases of data center equipment (servers, networking, power and cooling equipment, software), excluding electricity and construction equipment. Minimum capital investment is $450 million, $100 million or $25 million for owners, operators or colocation tenants, by county population, and $150 million for project organizers. Excluded projects include those accepting other KRS Chapter 154 incentives, replacing existing Commonwealth data centers, or benefiting from the electricity sales and use tax exemption for cryptocurrency mining. Agreement terms run 15 years (project organizers), 50 years (investment of at least $450 million) or 25 years (others). Sections 19-24, 26 and 35-37 take effect 1 July 2025. The excerpt does not show the exemption's operative tax rule or rate.

notes: Excerpt of the engrossed bill text (HB077520.100), an unofficial copy. Sections 1-33 and 35-39 are omitted, so the annotation covers Section 34 (definitions amending KRS 154.20-220) and Section 40 (effective dates) only. Text extraction is garbled in places (e.g., definitions (2), (4)-(8), (16) and (18)(b)2.), so quotes are taken from legible lines. Brackets in '(c)[' and '(d)]' under (17) appear to mark deleted text in the engrossed version. Section 40 makes Sections 19 to 24, 26, and 35 to 37 effective July 1, 2025; Section 34 is not listed and its effective date is not stated in the excerpt. Sub-item 1.c of (17)(b) reads 'Twenty-five million dollar ($25,000,000)'. No named firms appear in the excerpt.

County population is taken from the most recent five-year American Community Survey estimate at the time of application.
